root_cause: Two independent, previously-known recurring flaky tests failed on this Windows merge-queue run, unrelated to the PR's GPU-only changes (src/plugins/intel_gpu/...). (1) CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race exercises concurrent MULTI-device model loading against a GMock plugin; the mock's import_model EXPECT_CALL count is timing-sensitive and intermittently under-counts on loaded Windows CI runners because one of the racing load threads occasionally has not yet invoked import_model before the test's teardown/verification point. (2) TestKerasLSTM.test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 with dropout compares CPU-plugin inference output against TensorFlow's reference within a fixed epsilon; small, non-deterministic numerical drift from dropout-affected LSTM kernels intermittently exceeds the comparison tolerance. Neither failure touches code paths modified by PR #40019.
reproduction_steps: N/A (both are intermittent races/numerical-tolerance flakes not reliably reproducible locally; see historical pattern records 43e136cf67333978 (11 occurrences) and a284d27dfee44614 (10 occurrences) in /tmp/gh-aw/repo-memory/default/mq/patterns/ for prior occurrences and context).
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed jobs (C++ unit tests, TensorFlow Layer Tests) for this merge-queue run; both failures are known transient flakes unrelated to the PR diff.

Track CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race/ByModel_testCache for stabilization: either relax the EXPECT_CALL count to a range/minimum or add explicit synchronization so all racing load threads complete import_model before verification (src/inference/tests/functional/caching_test.cpp:2673, :318).

Track TestKerasLSTM.test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 dropout parametrization for either a wider epsilon or disabling dropout-active comparisons that are inherently non-deterministic (install/tests/layer_tests/tensorflow2_keras_tests/test_tf2_keras_lstm.py).
prevention_strategies: Both failures are long-standing known flaky tests already tracked in the CI Doctor MQ pattern database (counts 11 and 10). No new prevention action is required for this PR; continued tracking/escalation will occur automatically if recurrence accelerates within a 12-hour window.
